- Overestimate prices in early forecast windows, especially after recent spikes; reduce initial forecast values by 2–5%.
- Underestimate prices in late forecast windows; adjust upward by 1–3% if recent history shows sustained upward momentum.
- When true outcome exceeds forecast by >10% in 2–3 consecutive days, reduce subsequent forecasts by 3–5% to avoid overreaction.
- If forecast spikes sharply after a low, reduce the peak by 5–10% to account for market overcorrection.
- Mean-reversion bias: if forecast is >15% above 30-day moving average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- Lagged bias: if true outcome is consistently 2–3 days behind forecast, shift forecast down by 1–2% for the next 2–3 days.
- Avoid overfitting to recent high volatility; if 30-day history shows high variance, reduce forecast volatility by 10–15%.
- For low-price regimes (e.g., <75), forecast should not exceed 10% above recent 7-day average; cap forecasts at 10% above to avoid runaway spikes.
